import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_2.csv",

        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # List to hold dataframes
    dfs = []

    # Load each source CSV, ensure schema and types, then append to list
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

        # Enforce schema and types explicitly
        df = df[['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']]  # reorder columns if needed

        # Convert types according to target schema
        df['admit'] = df['admit'].astype(int)
        df['gre'] = df['gre'].astype(int)
        df['gpa'] = df['gpa'].astype(float)
        df['prestige'] = df['prestige'].astype(int)

        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source dataframes into one target dataframe
    target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Optional: If deduplication or sorting is needed, it can be done here.
    # The problem statement does not specify, so we keep all rows as is.

    # Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_94/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
